summary: The workflow declares least-privilege permissions (contents: read) - tighter than the harness-internal gate workflows, which rely on default token scopes. PR_BODY reaches the gate through env assignment, never interpolated into script text, so a hostile PR body cannot inject shell (same proven pattern as the internal workflow). The arming step reads only two repo files and fails closed on malformed JSON. The gates add enforcement and remove nothing: refusal paths stay refusals.
residual_risks: A PR can modify factory/scripts/check_pr_ticket.py in its own diff to neuter the PR job - a pre-existing class shared with every self-hosted CI check; in clients, vendor-integrity drift detection (harness-health) flags the tampered vendored file post-merge, and human review owns the PR diff itself.
The push audit executes repo code from the pushed ref; on the default branch that is post-merge code by definition.
